text:
maria: Customer (FinOpsCorp) asked for a Private/on-prem POC. They want a pre-install checklist we can hand to infra ops. Can we assemble the minimal validator checks (GPU drivers, CUDA, k8s, network) and any gotchas for secure-boot/air-gapped installs?

dan: +1. I'll need exact commands they should run to prove compatibility. Keep it short — ops will paste commands.

lee: Draft checklist below — feel free to trim. Mostly focused on NVIDIA stack + k8s basics and control-plane connectivity.

lee: 1) Kernel & NV drivers
- Verify kernel headers present: `uname -r` and corresponding `linux-headers-$(uname -r)` installed.
- Check NVIDIA driver is loaded: `lsmod | grep nvidia` (expect nvidia, nvidia_uvm).
- Confirm `nvidia-smi` runs and shows GPUs + driver version. Example output header: `Driver Version: 525.85.12`
- If secure boot is enabled, ensure drivers are signed or secure-boot disabled (common blocker).

lee: 2) CUDA / toolkit (if model vendors need it)
- Recommended minimum driver: NVIDIA >= 510 for CUDA 11.x, >= 525 for CUDA 12.x. For our current images we test against CUDA 11.8 and 12.1.
- Command: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,cuda_version --format=csv`

lee: 3) Container runtime & GPU plugin
- Confirm container runtime: `crictl --version` or `docker --version` or `containerd --version`. We recommend containerd (1.6+) or Docker Engine (20.10+) with nvidia-container-toolkit configured.
- Check NVIDIA container toolkit installed: `nvidia-container-cli info`
- For k8s: ensure NVIDIA device plugin daemonset is running: `kubectl get ds -n kube-system nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset`

lee: 4) Kubernetes compatibility
- Supported kubelet/kube-apiserver versions: 1.24–1.27 (our installer currently validated on these).
- Ensure swap is disabled: `sudo swapoff -a` and `sed -i '/ swap / s/^/#/' /etc/fstab`.
- Check cgroup driver: `ps -ef | grep kubelet` or `cat /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` -> prefer cgroupfs for Docker or systemd for containerd, ensure consistent across nodes.

lee: 5) Networking & control-plane reachability
- Private installs need outbound connectivity to our control-plane IPs or allow an IP range for SaaS control plane; provide list during onboarding.
- Open ports on nodes for control-plane agent: 443 outbound to our endpoints. If air-gapped, prepare image/tarball and offline registry.

lee: 6) Storage & kernel params
- Hugepages optional but recommended for certain models: `sysctl vm.nr_hugepages`
- File descriptor limits: ensure kubelet has high ulimit.

lee: 7) Security/Compliance notes
- If FIPS or strict HSM/KMS is required, note that extra config steps needed — collect KMS endpoint and certs ahead of time.
- Auditd/logging: we ship agents that forward logs; ask ops to whitelist agent IPs.

lee: Short commands bundle they can run and paste back:
```
uname -r
lsmod | grep nvidia || true
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,cuda_version --format=csv
docker --version || containerd --version
kubectl version --short
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl get ds -n kube-system nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset
sudo swapoff -a
```

sarah: Add: please include `dmesg | grep -i nvidia` and `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200` if they have bootstrap issues. Also ask them to confirm SELinux mode (`getenforce`) — we prefer Permissive or Disabled for now, otherwise we'll need to validate policies.

dan: For pricing/POC sizing — we typically recommend 1 dedicated GPU node for a quick smoke test (NVIDIA A10/A100 depending), + 1 control node. If they want throughput testing, ask for expected RPS and max sequence length so we can recommend pool size.

maria: Perfect — can we convert this into a one-page checklist and one-line commands they can paste? Also prep a short note for sales thread about secure-boot and air-gapped next steps.

deploy-bot: Installer v2.3 image (private-poc) available — use tag `redwood/poc-installer:v2.3` for offline tarball export.

lee: I'll make a TL;DR and drop in the repo + handoff doc. Will also add required control-plane IP list once legal signs the NDA.

maria: Thanks — I'll send to FinOpsCorp and ask for the command outputs. If they hit secure-boot, we'll schedule a quick run with eng on Wed. :thumbsup:
